package api

import (
	"time"

	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/trail"
)

// TrailListResponse is the response from GET /api/v1/trails/:org/:repo.
type TrailListResponse struct {
	Trails        []TrailResource `json:"trails"`
	RepoFullName  string          `json:"repo_full_name"`
	DefaultBranch string          `json:"default_branch"`
	UpdatedAt     time.Time       `json:"updated_at"`
}

// TrailResource represents a single trail from the API.
type TrailResource struct {
	Number          int              `json:"number,omitempty"`
	TrailID         string           `json:"trail_id"`
	Branch          string           `json:"branch"`
	Base            string           `json:"base"`
	Title           string           `json:"title"`
	Body            string           `json:"body"`
	Status          string           `json:"status"`
	Author          *trail.Author    `json:"author"`
	Assignees       []string         `json:"assignees"`
	Labels          []string         `json:"labels"`
	Priority        string           `json:"priority,omitempty"`
	Type            string           `json:"type,omitempty"`
	Reviewers       []trail.Reviewer `json:"reviewers,omitempty"`
	CreatedAt       time.Time        `json:"created_at"`
	UpdatedAt       time.Time        `json:"updated_at"`
	MergedAt        *time.Time       `json:"merged_at,omitempty"`
	CommentCount    int              `json:"comment_count,omitempty"`
	UnresolvedCount int              `json:"unresolved_count,omitempty"`
	CheckpointCount int              `json:"checkpoint_count,omitempty"`
	CommitsAhead    int              `json:"commits_ahead,omitempty"`
}

// ToMetadata converts a TrailResource to a trail.Metadata for display.
func (r *TrailResource) ToMetadata() *trail.Metadata {
	m := &trail.Metadata{
		Number:    r.Number,
		TrailID:   trail.ID(r.TrailID),
		Branch:    r.Branch,
		Base:      r.Base,
		Title:     r.Title,
		Body:      r.Body,
		Status:    trail.Status(r.Status),
		Author:    r.Author,
		Assignees: r.Assignees,
		Labels:    r.Labels,
		Priority:  trail.Priority(r.Priority),
		Type:      trail.Type(r.Type),
		Reviewers: r.Reviewers,
		CreatedAt: r.CreatedAt,
		UpdatedAt: r.UpdatedAt,
		MergedAt:  r.MergedAt,
	}
	if m.Assignees == nil {
		m.Assignees = []string{}
	}
	if m.Labels == nil {
		m.Labels = []string{}
	}
	return m
}

// TrailCreateRequest is the body for POST /api/v1/trails/:host/:owner/:repo.
type TrailCreateRequest struct {
	Title      string   `json:"title"`
	Body       string   `json:"body,omitempty"`
	BranchName string   `json:"branch_name"`
	Base       string   `json:"base,omitempty"`
	Status     string   `json:"status,omitempty"`
	Assignees  []string `json:"assignees,omitempty"`
	Labels     []string `json:"labels,omitempty"`
	Priority   string   `json:"priority,omitempty"`
	Type       string   `json:"type,omitempty"`

content.text:
Updated:

- Removed the “show all” behavior (`--limit 0` is no longer valid).
- Removed the `--all` flag from `trail list`.
- Added `--mine` to switch from “most recent trails” to “my most recent trails”.
- Kept `--limit` as a positive max count only.
- `--status` can still explicitly show a status like `merged` or `closed`.
- Branch remains untruncated; title truncates instead.

Verified with:

```sh
mise exec -- go test ./cmd/entire/cli
```
I want options to return the list filtered by author and/or status. Default should be "me" and in_progress. Recommend a parameter design.

Recommended design:

```sh
entire trail list [--author <author>] [--status <status>] [--limit <n>]
```

Defaults:

```sh
--author me
--status in_progress
--limit 10
```

Examples:

```sh
entire trail list
# my 10 most recent in_progress trails

entire trail list --author alice
# alice’s 10 most recent in_progress trails

entire trail list --author any
# any author’s 10 most recent in_progress trails

entire trail list --status open
# my 10 most recent open trails

entire trail list --author any --status any
# 10 most recent trails across all authors/statuses
```

Author values:

- `me` — authenticated user, default
- `any` / `all` — no author filter
- `<login>` — filter by specific author login

Status values:

- `in_progress` — default
- `draft`
- `open`
- `in_review`
- `merged`
- `closed`
- `active` — optional alias for non-terminal statuses: `draft,open,in_progress,in_review`
- `any` / `all` — no status filter

I’d avoid separate flags like `--mine`, `--all`, `--active`; they don’t compose as cleanly. One `--author` and one `--status` gives predictable filtering and scales better.
Where come the open/closed/active states from? Just use the ones from trails.

Agreed. Use only trail statuses from `trail.ValidStatuses()`:

```sh
entire trail list [--author <author>] [--status <status>] [--limit <n>]
```

Defaults:

```sh
--author me
--status in_progress
--limit 10
```

Author values:

- `me` — authenticated user, default
- `<login>` — specific author login

For “any author”, I’d use an empty/no filter value:

```sh
entire trail list --author ""
```

or, cleaner if you prefer explicit:

```sh
entire trail list --author "*"
```

Status values: exactly the trail statuses already defined in code:

- `draft`
- `open`
- `in_progress`
- `in_review`
- `merged`
- `closed`

For “any status”, same design choice:

```sh
entire trail list --status ""
```

or explicit wildcard:

```sh
entire trail list --status "*"
```

I’d recommend `*` for “no filter” because defaults are filtered, and it’s explicit:

```sh
entire trail list
# me + in_progress

entire trail list --author alice
# alice + in_progress

entire trail list --status open
# me + open

entire trail list --author "*" --status "*"
# most recent trails, any author/status
```
What if not providing an "any" value and just e.g. "--author" and show any then?

Yes, that’s a good CLI design if implemented as an optional-value flag:

```sh
entire trail list --author
```

means “disable the default author filter / any author”.

Then:

```sh
entire trail list
# author=me, status=in_progress

entire trail list --author alice
# author=alice, status=in_progress

entire trail list --author --status open
# any author, status=open

entire trail list --status
# author=me, any status

entire trail list --author --status
# any author, any status
```

Caveat: optional-value flags can be slightly surprising with Cobra/pflag. You’d need `NoOptDefVal`, e.g.:

```go
cmd.Flags().StringVar(&author, "author", "me", "Filter by author login; omit value for any author")
cmd.Flags().Lookup("author").NoOptDefVal = ""
```

Same for status:

```go
cmd.Flags().StringVar(&status, "status", "in_progress", "Filter by status; omit value for any status")
cmd.Flags().Lookup("status").NoOptDefVal = ""
```

I’d recommend this design. It keeps the default useful, avoids fake `any/all/*` status values, and stays composable.

content.text:
Implemented.

Parameter design now:

```sh
entire trail list
# default: --author me --status in_progress --limit 10

entire trail list --author alice
# alice + in_progress

entire trail list --author
# any author + in_progress

entire trail list --status open
# me + open

entire trail list --status
# me + any status

entire trail list --author --status
# any author + any status, grouped by trail status
```

Changes:
- Added `--author` optional-value flag.
- Changed `--status` to default to `in_progress` and optional-value for any status.
- Removed `--mine`.
- Uses only existing `trail.ValidStatuses()`.
- Updated human-readable output to match the requested compact style.
- Groups by status when status filter is omitted.
- Keeps `--json` returning the filtered/limited list.

Verified:

```sh
mise exec -- go test ./cmd/entire/cli
```
Create a PR with description of the changes and the new output design.

## Summary

- Change `entire trail list` from an unbounded/all-trails table to a recent-trails view capped by `--limit` (default: 10).
- Add composable `--author` and `--status` filters with useful defaults:
  - `--author me`
  - `--status in_progress`
- Support optional-value filters:
  - `--author` with no value disables author filtering (any author)
  - `--status` with no value disables status filtering (any trail status)
- Remove the previous `--all`/`--mine` style behavior in favor of explicit filter composition.
- Keep branches untruncated in output and move away from the old title/status/author table for the compact list design.

Default: your recent in-progress trails.

```console
$ entire trail list
  Your trails · 6 in progress

  feat/explain-fetch-progress               1d ago
  feat/explain-streaming-diagnostic         1d ago
  feat/openai-privacy-filter-v1-backup      2d ago
  feat/openai-privacy-filter                2d ago
  slow-codex-in-review                      3d ago
  redact-2                                  3d ago
```

```console
$ entire trail list --author alice
  alice · 4 in progress

  feat/cohort-analysis                      2d ago
  feat/billing-webhooks                     3d ago
  fix/timezone-edge-cases                   5d ago
  chore/upgrade-postgres-driver             1w ago
```

```console
  In progress · 10 trails
```

**Determining status order**

I'm considering how to structure a status display for group orders. The user mentioned using statuses from trails, but I'm realizing that the display order may need to reflect the most recent occurrences, which might conflict with their preferred order. 

I think it could be effective to display statuses like this: in_progress, open, in_review, draft, merged, closed. I'm also keeping in mind their feedback about prioritizing certain statuses, so let's ensure we implement that function to create a clear trail list status order.

**Clarifying API structure**

I'm thinking about how tests can assert that "In progress" appears before "Open." It seems like I need to understand the actual shape of the /api/v1/me endpoint. Maybe focusing on activity could help, and I wonder if I could streamline it using one field. Unfortunately, I can't find the API documentation right now, and if I decode `login`, it could be risky if the API returns a username. Maybe using an existing server shape would be better? The user did mention the backend, so that’s something to consider.

## Summary

- Change `entire trail list` from an unbounded/all-trails table to a recent-trails view capped by `--limit` (default: 10).
- Add composable `--author` and `--status` filters with useful defaults:
  - `--author me`
  - `--status in_progress`
- Support optional-value filters:
  - `--author` with no value disables author filtering (any author)
  - `--status` with no value disables status filtering (any trail status)
- Remove the previous `--all`/`--mine` style behavior in favor of explicit filter composition.
- Keep branches untruncated in output and move away from the old title/status/author table for the compact list design.

## New output design

Default: your recent in-progress trails.

```console
$ entire trail list
  Your trails · 6 in progress

  feat/explain-fetch-progress               1d ago
  feat/explain-streaming-diagnostic         1d ago
  feat/openai-privacy-filter-v1-backup      2d ago

  slow-codex-in-review                      3d ago
  redact-2                                  3d ago
```

```console
$ entire trail list --author alice
  alice · 4 in progress

  feat/cohort-analysis                      2d ago
  feat/billing-webhooks                     3d ago
  fix/timezone-edge-cases                   5d ago
  chore/upgrade-postgres-driver             1w ago
```

Any author, default status (`in_progress`):

```console
  In progress · 10 trails

```

Default author (`me`), specific status:

```console

  Your trails · 8 open

  feat/throttle-runner-spawn                4d ago
```

```console
  Recent trails · 10
```

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes default CLI behavior and adds an extra `/api/v1/me` call to resolve `--author me`, which could affect UX and API error paths but is contained to trail listing.
> 
> **Overview**
> `entire trail list` now defaults to a **recent trails** view (capped by `--limit`, default 10) instead of listing everything, and the root `entire trail` fallback now shows this recent view when no trail exists for the current branch.
> 
> Replaces the old `--all` behavior with composable `--author` and `--status` filters (both support optional/no-value to disable filtering), resolves `--author me` via a new `/api/v1/me` lookup, and updates the non-JSON output to a compact, untruncated branch list that can optionally include author and/or group results by status.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/390
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

- Change `entire trail list` from an unbounded/all-trails table to a recent-trails view capped by `--limit` (default: 10).
- Make the default view repository-wide in-progress trails:
  - author filter defaults to any author
  - status filter defaults to `in_progress`
- Add composable filters:
  - `--author <login>` filters by author
  - `--author me` treats `me` as an alias for the authenticated user's username
  - `--author` with no value disables author filtering explicitly
  - `--status <status[,status...]>` filters by one or more comma-separated trail statuses
  - `--status` with no value disables status filtering
- Remove the previous `--all` behavior in favor of explicit filter composition.
- Keep branches untruncated and render a compact branch/author/age list instead of the old title/status/author table.

## New output design

Default: recent in-progress trails for the repo.

```console
$ entire trail list
  In progress · 10 trails

  feat/explain-fetch-progress                    peyton-alt      1d ago
  dependabot/…/codeql-action-4.35.5              dependabot      1d ago
  feat/explain-streaming-diagnostic              peyton-alt      1d ago
  fix/checkpoints-v2-full-transcript-fallback    pfleidi         1d ago
  feat/openai-privacy-filter-v1-backup           peyton-alt      2d ago
  soph/better-migration-email                    Soph            2d ago
  feat/openai-privacy-filter                     peyton-alt      2d ago
  fix-slow-v2-pushes                             computermode    3d ago
  slow-codex-in-review                           peyton-alt      3d ago
  redact-2                                       peyton-alt      3d ago
```

Your trails via `--author me`:

```console
$ entire trail list --author me
  Your trails · 6 in progress

  feat/explain-fetch-progress               1d ago
  feat/explain-streaming-diagnostic         1d ago
  feat/openai-privacy-filter-v1-backup      2d ago
  feat/openai-privacy-filter                2d ago
  slow-codex-in-review                      3d ago
  redact-2                                  3d ago
```

Specific author, default status (`in_progress`):

```console
$ entire trail list --author alice
  alice · 4 in progress

  feat/cohort-analysis                      2d ago
  feat/billing-webhooks                     3d ago
  fix/timezone-edge-cases                   5d ago
  chore/upgrade-postgres-driver             1w ago
```

Comma-separated statuses:

```console
$ entire trail list --status open,closed
  Open, closed · 10 trails

  Open · 8

  redact-2                                  peyton-alt      1d ago
  slow-codex-in-review                      peyton-alt      3d ago
  feat/throttle-runner-spawn                peyton-alt      4d ago
  feat/new-experiment                       Soph            5d ago
  fix/runner-timeout-handling               computermode    6d ago
  chore/bump-deps                           dependabot      1w ago
  feat/checkpoint-pagination                alice           1w ago
  fix/sse-keepalive                         Kai             2w ago

  Closed · 2

  feat/checkpoint-search                    pfleidi         2h ago
  fix/sse-reconnect                         Kai             5h ago
```

Any author, any status groups the limited recent results by existing trail statuses:

```console
$ entire trail list --author --status
  Recent trails · 10

  In progress · 5

  feat/explain-fetch-progress         peyton-alt      1d ago
  feat/explain-streaming-diagnostic   peyton-alt      1d ago
  soph/better-migration-email         Soph            2d ago
  feat/openai-privacy-filter          peyton-alt      2d ago
  slow-codex-in-review                peyton-alt      3d ago

  Open · 3

  redact-2                            peyton-alt      1d ago
  feat/cohort-analysis                alice           1d ago
  feat/throttle-runner-spawn          peyton-alt      4d ago

  Closed · 2

  feat/checkpoint-search              pfleidi         2h ago
  fix/sse-reconnect                   Kai             5h ago
```

## Testing

```console
mise exec -- go test ./cmd/entire/cli
mise run lint:go
```
